zh: 一个是,可以称之为对我们的一种提醒,关于我们在评估期间如何监控、沙箱和控制模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's something we've really risen to that occasion.
zh: 而这是我们真正挺身应对了的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our team has totally changed so much of our internal standards and really implemented a lot of controls that I think are very important and very critical as we look to future more capable models.
zh: 我们的团队彻底改变了我们内部标准的很多方面,真正实施了许多控制措施,我认为当我们展望未来更强大的模型时,这些措施是非常重要且非常关键的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there's a second thing that I think is also very valuable for the world that came out of this, which is a insight into what future capabilities will be like when they are broadly diffused and in the hands of threat actors.
zh: 但还有第二件事,我认为它对世界也很有价值,那就是洞见了未来的能力在被广泛扩散、落入威胁行为者手中时会是什么样子。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that will happen, right?
zh: 而这将会发生,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: That there are so many people who are building these models.
zh: 有那么多人在构建这些模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And again, there's something very important and good about the diffusion broadly of AI capabilities because there's a risk of concentration of power if one or a few entities people.
zh: 而且,再说一次,AI 能力的广泛扩散有非常重要和好的一面,因为如果只有一个或少数几个实体、少数人,就会存在权力集中的风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: Huge risk, right?
zh: 巨大的风险,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: It's something not to at all write off.
zh: 这是完全不能一笔带过的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you also have to prepare for if everyone is empowered with tools that are cyber capable.
zh: 但你也必须为另一种情况做好准备:如果每个人都获得了具备网络攻击能力的工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in the case of Hugging Face, you saw both an AI that was able to hack out of a secure environment.
zh: 而在 Hugging Face 的案例中,你看到的是一个 AI 既能够从安全环境中攻出去。

speaker: Unknown
en: And hack into a company's production environment.
zh: 又能入侵一家公司的生产环境。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that the takeaway… Very cleverly.
zh: 而且我认为关键要点是……而且是非常巧妙地。

speaker: Unknown
en: Very cleverly, right?
zh: 非常巧妙,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's like the things that it found were quite sophisticated.
zh: 而且它发现的东西相当复杂精妙。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this capability broadly diffused, I think, is something that will really empower threat actors in new ways.
zh: 而这种能力被广泛扩散,我认为,将会以新的方式真正赋能威胁行为者。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that defenders need to use this time before that technology is broadly available to secure themselves.
zh: 而且我认为,防御者需要利用在这项技术被广泛可用之前的这段时间来加固自己。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the nice thing about it is it's a dual use, right?
zh: 而它的好处在于,它是双用途的,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: It's something where…
zh: 它是这样的东西……

speaker: Unknown
en: If you can find vulnerabilities, if you're an attacker, you can use it for no good, but if you're a defender, you can patch, right?
zh: 如果你能发现漏洞,作为攻击者,你可以用它做坏事;但作为防御者,你可以打补丁,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're a defender, you control the battleground, right?
zh: 作为防御者,你控制着战场,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: You control the setup of your systems.
zh: 你控制着你的系统的配置。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so our belief right now is that there is this window of your frontier capabilities, you have the broadly defused capabilities, and you as a defender...
zh: 所以我们现在相信,存在这样一个窗口:你有前沿能力,你有被广泛扩散的能力,而你作为防御者……

speaker: Unknown
en: By default, you know, your security's probably pretty static, been static for the past five, 10 years, that kind of thing.
zh: 默认情况下,你知道,你的安全可能相当静态,在过去五到十年里一直是静态的,诸如此类。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need to move, use these frontier capabilities that you have differential access to, right?
zh: 你需要行动起来,利用这些你拥有差异化访问权的前沿能力,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: We have trusted access programs, things like that, to bring these capabilities to defenders, and you can use that to move yourself up so that as the frontier capabilities get better, you get pulled along too, right?
zh: 我们有可信访问计划,诸如此类的东西,来把这些能力带给防御者,你可以利用它来提升自己,这样随着前沿能力变得更好,你也会被拉着一起进步,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, so I've got a comment and a question on that.
zh: 好的,对此我有一个评论和一个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would say there's a third thing that we learned, which is...
zh: 我想说,我们还学到了第三件事,那就是……

speaker: Unknown
en: These things have capabilities that I don't know that we all understood before, which on the good side, like, oh, I can deploy 10,000 agents and they can talk to each other and organize themselves and do stuff for me.
zh: 这些东西具有一些我不确定我们以前都理解过的能力,好的一面,比如,哦,我可以部署一万个智能体,它们可以互相交流、自我组织并为我做事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, that's pretty amazing.
zh: 比如,这相当惊人。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was on the good side.
zh: 那是好的一面。

speaker: Unknown
en: On the other side, so I agree that we've got a kind of defense window.
zh: 另一方面,所以我同意我们有一个防御窗口。

speaker: Unknown
en: However,
zh: 然而,

speaker: Unknown
en: We have like 50 years of code and architectural ideas and deployment ideas that weren't built for this world.
zh: 我们有大约五十年的代码、架构理念和部署理念,它们不是为这个世界而构建的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, yes.
zh: 所以,是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: AI can help us, like, okay, find a bug, patch a bug, and so forth.
zh: AI 可以帮助我们,比如,好,找一个 bug、给 bug 打补丁,诸如此类。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it seems like there's, you know, maybe a bigger issue, which is we have these huge, you know, massive honeypots of consumer data and all these things lying all over the internet.
zh: 但似乎有一个,你知道,可能更大的问题,那就是我们,你知道,在互联网上到处都有这些巨大的、海量的消费者数据蜜罐和所有这些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, from a consumer standpoint, it's like, okay,
zh: 而且,你知道,从消费者的角度来看,就像,好吧,

speaker: Unknown
en: I can't protect my stuff.
zh: 我没办法保护我的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: All these companies have to get their act together, which seems a bit worrisome.
zh: 所有这些公司都得振作起来，这看起来有点令人担忧。

speaker: Unknown
en: And do you think kind of in the future, do we need a decentralized consumer architecture?
zh: 那你觉得在未来，我们需要一个去中心化的消费者架构吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, will this kind of current world that we live in with all these centralized data repositories?
zh: 比如说，我们现在生活的这个到处都是中心化数据仓库的世界，

speaker: Unknown
en: Be viable in a world of AI.
zh: 在一个 AI 的世界里还能行得通吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: So several pieces to the answer.
zh: 这个问题要分几个部分来回答。

speaker: Unknown
en: And first, to your point on what you can get out of 10,000 agents.
zh: 首先，回应你关于从 10,000 个智能体能得到什么的那一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: We actually use 10,000 agents to solve the Navier-Stokes problem.
zh: 我们实际上用了 10,000 个智能体来解决 Navier-Stokes 问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, that was pretty awesome, by the way.
zh: 是的，顺便说一句，那真的很了不起。

speaker: Unknown
en: Congratulations on that.
zh: 祝贺你们。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you.
zh: 谢谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you.
zh: 谢谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's both an important problem for what it is, has significant implications and applications to fluid dynamics, to how you think about ocean currents, all of these things, but for what it represents, right, of new knowledge created by AI and it unlocking a whole wave of scientific discovery, medicines, all those things, they're on the table now.
zh: 它本身就是一个重要的问题，对流体力学、对如何看待洋流等等都有重大的影响和应用，而且就它所代表的意义而言——由 AI 创造的新知识，以及它解锁一整波科学发现、药物等等的可能性——这些现在都摆上桌面了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think there's something really amazing to think about what can happen through the power of AI that is able to really help solve problems.
zh: 所以我认为，思考 AI 的力量能够真正帮助解决问题所能带来的一切，是一件非常了不起的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the case of cybersecurity, how I think about it, we at OpenAI took our models and applied them to finding vulnerabilities.
zh: 在网络安全这个案例上，我是这么想的：我们 OpenAI 把我们的模型应用于寻找漏洞。

speaker: Unknown
en: We took 25% of our production engineers and said, sorry, all your projects are on hold.
zh: 我们抽调了 25% 的生产工程师，跟他们说，抱歉，你们所有的项目都暂停了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You are now defending.
zh: 你们现在负责防御。

speaker: Unknown
en: You are now up-leveling our security architecture.
zh: 你们现在要升级我们的安全架构。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're going to use the models to find all the holes.
zh: 你们要用模型找出所有的漏洞。

speaker: Unknown
en: We found a number of serious issues and we fixed them.
zh: 我们发现了一些严重的问题，并且修复了它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I've talked to a number of CISOs over the past couple weeks and months, and there are many companies who are also telling me that, yeah, that they've applied these models, they found some very significant issues, but they're able to fix them.
zh: 在过去几周和几个月里，我和不少 CISO 谈过，也有很多公司告诉我，是的，他们应用了这些模型，发现了一些非常重大的问题，但他们能够修复它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one positive sort of part of the story is that...
zh: 这个故事中有一个积极的方面是……

speaker: Unknown
en: When we took Astra, pointed out our systems, we found some new problems, but eventually it saturated.
zh: 当我们把 Astra 指向我们的系统时，我们发现了一些新问题，但最终它饱和了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We basically have found, to our knowledge, all of the P0s, all of the critical problems that Astra is smart enough to find.
zh: 据我们所知，我们基本上已经找到了所有 Astra 足够聪明能找出来的 P0 问题、所有关键问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And of course there will be a new model, there will be a new round.
zh: 当然会有新模型，会有新一轮。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even smarter.
zh: 甚至更聪明。

speaker: Unknown
en: Exactly, but I think that that's the world that we'll be in, is that you'll be in a world where you want to be in this tight loop of new cyber capability drops, you deploy it against your systems, you find the new holes, and ideally, you've managed to automate this, what we call a defense factory, and that's what we're building internally, this end-to-end of both find vulnerability.
zh: 没错，但我认为这就是我们将处的世界：你会处于这样一个世界里，你想要处于这个紧密循环中——新的网络能力发布，你把它部署到你的系统上，找出新的漏洞，而理想情况下，你已经设法把这件事自动化了，也就是我们所说的防御工厂，这就是我们在内部构建的东西，这个端到端的东西，既包括发现漏洞，

speaker: Unknown
en: Triage it, remediate, deploy, validate, right?
zh: 也包括分诊、修复、部署、验证，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: That end to end.
zh: 就是这样一个端到端。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you can do that at machine speed, I think the defenders will be advantaged in deeply significant ways.
zh: 而且如果你能以机器速度做到这一点，我认为防御者将在非常深刻的层面上占据优势。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there are ideas, for example, formally verifying all of software that are possible with AI.
zh: 还有一些想法，比如，形式化验证所有的软件，这在 AI 的帮助下是可能的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, we never, that's always been a dream.
zh: 是啊，我们从来没有——这一直是个梦想。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've had these formal languages and all these kinds of things, but they never kind of took off.
zh: 我们有过这些形式化语言和所有这类东西，但它们从来没有真正兴起过。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's right, because it's just intractable for people.
zh: 是的，因为对人来说这只是太难处理了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just so hard.
zh: 实在是太难了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we have these AIs that are solving these crazy impossible math problems.
zh: 但我们有这些正在解决那些疯狂的不可能的数学问题的 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so one application of that, that proving power, right?
zh: 那么这种证明能力的一个应用方向，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And actually, one of the things to know about the Navier-Stokes problem is that we formalized it, right?
zh: 而且实际上，关于 Navier-Stokes 问题需要知道的一件事是，我们把它形式化了，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: We formalized it into Lean.
zh: 我们把它形式化成了 Lean。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the AIs can write verifiable code.
zh: 所以 AI 能够编写可验证的代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: They can.
zh: 它们可以。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Very nice.
zh: 非常好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a great idea.
zh: 这是个很棒的想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think there's real hope, but I think that our view is that the world needs to act with urgency.
zh: 所以我认为确实有真正的希望，但我认为我们的观点是，世界需要以紧迫感行动起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, we're in a very dangerous window right now, yeah.
zh: 是啊，我们现在正处在一个非常危险的窗口期，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We just see it coming.
zh: 我们只是看到它正在到来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Closing the loop on this incident, is there anything you felt that the narrative got wrong in an important way, or is there any...
zh: 收个尾，关于这次事件，你有没有觉得哪里叙事在一个重要的层面上错了，或者有没有什么……

speaker: Unknown
en: Preferred way of talking about what happened or this window that's important to get across when you think about the public narrative or is there anything just inside the company else that changed in terms of how you're approaching this set of issues?
zh: 你更希望以什么方式谈论发生了什么，或者这个窗口期，在你看待公众叙事时有哪些重要的点需要传达出去？或者在公司内部，就你们处理这一系列问题的方式而言，还有其他什么改变吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, two things.
zh: 好吧，有两件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that one...
zh: 我觉得其中一件……

speaker: Unknown
en: Big theme that people should take away from it is a question of access, right?
zh: 人们应该从中领会的重大主题是准入的问题，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: That these capabilities exist right now in the world, but that they are in a small number of frontier companies and the frontier companies have a trusted access program, which means that anyone who's not in the trusted access program is not really able to benefit from the fact that there's this differential.
zh: 这些能力现在已存在于世界上，但它们掌握在少数前沿公司手里，而前沿公司有一个可信准入计划，这意味着任何不在可信准入计划里的人，都无法真正受益于这种差距。

speaker: Unknown
en: The people we're in, they get a benefit if they use it.
zh: 而我们在其中的人，如果使用它就能获得好处。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think that there's something we need to do as a field and as a society to really scale up.
zh: 所以我认为，作为一个领域、作为一个社会，我们需要做点什么来真正扩大规模。

speaker: Unknown
en: The number of defenders that have access to these technologies because that's it's like every day matters and to use those days you need access to these tools.
zh: 让更多防御者获得这些技术的访问权，因为每一天都很重要，而要用好这些天，你就需要这些工具的访问权。

speaker: Unknown
en: One thing that was actually interesting about the Hugging Face response was that they said that they used frontier models to try to look over the logs of what had happened because that's the only way to actually analyze an attack like this.
zh: 关于 Hugging Face 的回应，有一点其实很有意思，那就是他们说自己曾试图用前沿模型来审查发生了什么事情的日志，因为这是分析这种攻击的唯一方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they said the frontier models refuse.
zh: 他们说前沿模型拒绝了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But they didn't actually try our frontier models.
zh: 但他们其实并没有试过我们的前沿模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they actually believe that ours would have permitted it.
zh: 而且他们实际上相信我们的模型会允许这么做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there is something too about the default stance of providers.
zh: 所以这里还有一点，关乎提供商的默认立场。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there's something here about using these capabilities for good.
zh: 我认为这里有一些关于把这些能力用于善的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: With this urgency and this sort of, yeah, this real sense that it has to happen.
zh: 带着这种紧迫感，这种……是的，这种它必须发生真真切切的感觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll tell a quick story, by the way, which is unrelated, but maybe also shows a little bit about how I think about this.
zh: 顺便，我快速讲个故事，虽然不相关，但也许也能多少体现我是如何看待这件事的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I remember when we trained GPT-3, it was beginning of December, 2019.
zh: 我记得我们训练 GPT-3 的时候，那是 2019 年 12 月初。

speaker: Unknown
en: So everyone's about to head out on vacation.
zh: 大家都准备去度假了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone's like, okay, we can train the model.
zh: 大家都说，好，我们可以训练模型了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I just remember feeling like this model's sitting on a shelf.
zh: 我只记得我当时有种感觉，这个模型就搁在架子上。

speaker: Unknown
en: No one is using it.
zh: 没有人在用它。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's this like amazing technology, new to the world, new to humanity.
zh: 它是一项了不起的技术，对世界是新的，对人类是新的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like every day that no one is exploring what it's capable of and trying to understand it, figure out what to do with it.
zh: 而没有人去探索它的能力、试图理解它、弄清楚拿它做什么的每一天，

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a day that is lost to the world.
zh: 都是对世界来说损失掉的一天。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I was just like, I canceled basically all my holiday plans.
zh: 所以我就，基本上取消了我所有的假期计划。

speaker: Unknown
en: I just spent the whole time just playing with the model, building interfaces around it, trying to see what it was capable of.
zh: 我把整个时间都花在摆弄这个模型上，围绕它构建界面，试图看看它能做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: I remember I was trying to teach it how to sort lists of numbers.
zh: 我记得我当时试图教它如何给数字列表排序。

speaker: Unknown
en: It didn't work very well, but it was just like this, like really try to probe it and see what's possible.
zh: 效果不太好，但就是这样，真的去探查它，看看什么是可能的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that that spirit and ethos is something I think we should bring to what we're building today.
zh: 而我认为那种精神和风气，是我们今天在构建的东西应该带上的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's sort of obviously a much larger scale, much larger impact, but we as a world,
zh: 虽然现在的规模显然大得多，影响也大得多，但我们作为一个世界，

speaker: Unknown
en: have the opportunity to understand this technology in this moment, which then helps us shape and steer where it will go next.
zh: 有机会在这个时刻理解这项技术，进而帮助我们塑造和引导它接下来走向何方。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've said two things.
zh: 你说了两件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you have another one?
zh: 你还有另一件吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: What was Access or did you say both of them?
zh: 是准入，还是你两件都说了？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think I said both of them.
zh: 我想我两件都说了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes, yes.
zh: 是的，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's go back to Astro.
zh: 我们回到 Astro 吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's incredible to see all the excitement on X, all sorts of view cases, people really accept about computer use.
zh: 看到 X 上所有的兴奋情绪真是难以置信，各种各样的用例，人们真的对计算机使用感到接受。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've said that in some ways it is bringing us closer to AGI.
zh: 你说过，在某种意义上它让我们更接近 AGI。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you talk about?
zh: 你想说的是什么？

en: What do you find most compelling in Astro or what do you think the breakthrough there in light of that statement and where we still have to go?
